findings.highlight: does not bear any memories of the victory
findings.evidenceJa: 勝利の余韻もなく
findings.governingReading: She feels no lingering afterglow of victory.
findings.explanation: The English turns the absence of present emotional afterglow into an absence of memories.

findings.highlight: I think about such random things.
findings.evidenceJa: 呆れるほど見当違いなコトを、思っていた
findings.governingReading: He had been thinking something astonishingly far off the mark.
findings.explanation: The English removes the scene’s explicit reversal of Shirou’s initial interpretation and calls his connected inference random.

findings.highlight: Just a cold truth that cannot be changed.
findings.evidenceJa: 冷たい過去に他ならない
findings.governingReading: the cold past, read as “reality,” that can no longer be changed
findings.explanation: The English discards the explicit past/reality doubleness and substitutes generic truth.

findings.highlight: After becoming a feudal lord like her father
findings.evidenceJa: 父に代わって領主となった後
findings.governingReading: After becoming lord in place of her father
findings.explanation: Like changes succession or substitution into resemblance and blurs how Arturia assumes rule.

findings.highlight: the girl with childlike features
findings.evidenceJa: まだ幼さを残していた少女
findings.governingReading: the girl who was still young
findings.explanation: The English turns her remaining youth into a judgment about physical facial features.

findings.highlight: the loud round table filled with the knights’ tales of bravado
findings.evidenceJa: 騎士たちが各々に武勇を語る華やかな円卓
findings.governingReading: the splendid Round Table where the knights recount their martial exploits
findings.explanation: Bravado imputes boastful posturing and weakens the public fellowship from which the king is excluded.

findings.highlight: She was only idolized.
findings.evidenceJa: 彼女はただ、偶像として容認されただけだった
findings.governingReading: She was merely tolerated or accepted as an idol.
findings.explanation: Idolized reverses conditional, dehumanizing acceptance into positive adoration.

findings.highlight: Arturia who looked like a small kid
findings.evidenceJa: 少年の姿であるアルトリア
findings.governingReading: Arturia in the form of a boy
findings.explanation: The English erases the gendered public guise and replaces it with diminutive age language.

findings.highlight: She brought peace to the fighting lords
findings.evidenceJa: 争い合っていた領主たちをまとめ上げ
findings.governingReading: She united the lords who had been fighting one another.
findings.explanation: The English weakens Arturia’s political consolidation into an abstract peace she brought to the lords.

findings.highlight: fought off the invading enemies
findings.evidenceJa: 侵攻してくる異民族を撃退した
findings.governingReading: repelled the invading foreign peoples
findings.explanation: The English removes the historical identity of the invaders and generalizes them into enemies.

findings.highlight: She worked hard
findings.evidenceJa: 文字通り身を粉にして
findings.governingReading: She literally ground herself down to remain the ideal king.
findings.explanation: Worked hard erases the bodily self-destruction in Arturia’s performance of perfect kingship.

findings.highlight: It was only natural for them to trample over them
findings.evidenceJa: それらは蹂躙されて当然のものであり
findings.governingReading: The knights regard those villages as naturally destined to be overrun by the enemy.
findings.explanation: The English makes the knights themselves trample the villages, changing the actor in the hypocrisy being described.

findings.highlight: a revolt against the king
findings.evidenceJa: 王への反感だった
findings.governingReading: resentment toward the king
findings.explanation: The English promotes an accumulating attitude into an organized political event before the text reaches open collapse.

findings.highlight: They pushed all problems onto her
findings.evidenceJa: あらゆる外敵と自国の問題を押しつけ
findings.governingReading: They thrust every foreign enemy and every domestic problem onto her.
findings.explanation: The English drops the exhaustive external/internal burden that explains how the knights corner the king.

findings.highlight: A scene from a few years before.
findings.evidenceJa: もう何年も昔になった光景
findings.governingReading: A scene already many years in the past.
findings.explanation: Few compresses the elapsed span and contradicts 何年も.

findings.highlight: the brave sounds of the cavalry
findings.evidenceJa: 勇ましい騎兵の音
findings.governingReading: the gallant sound of cavalry in the distance
findings.explanation: Brave sounds is malformed and transfers a human quality to the noise itself.

findings.highlight: He says he is not trying to frighten her, but that she should stop.
findings.evidenceJa: 悪い事は言わないから止めておけ
findings.governingReading: He advises her to stop, saying he would not steer her wrong.
findings.explanation: The English invents a denial of frightening intent and loses Merlin’s idiom of well-meant warning.

findings.highlight: She takes the sword.
findings.evidenceJa: 剣に手をかける
findings.governingReading: She lays her hand on the sword.
findings.explanation: The English prematurely turns touching the sword into taking possession of it before the decisive draw.

findings.highlight: The magus turns his back
findings.evidenceJa: 魔術師は困ったように顔を背け
findings.governingReading: The magus averts his face, looking troubled.
findings.explanation: The English changes a facial withdrawal into a full-body turn and omits Merlin’s troubled expression.

findings.highlight: She threw away her heart.
findings.evidenceJa: 人としての心は捨てた
findings.governingReading: She cast aside her heart as a human being.
findings.explanation: The English makes Arturia discard her entire capacity for feeling rather than the human heart incompatible with her constructed kingship.

findings.highlight: No matter what.
findings.evidenceJa: 何があろうと、たとえ、その先に
findings.governingReading: No matter what happened, even if what lay ahead—
findings.explanation: The English drops the suspended condition whose interruption and later completion shape the oath’s rhythm and foreknowledge.

findings.highlight: her country split into two, and a war began
findings.evidenceJa: 国は二つに分かれて殺し合った
findings.governingReading: the country split in two and its people killed one another
findings.explanation: The English weakens explicit civil slaughter into the mere beginning of a war.

findings.highlight: were utterly destroyed
findings.evidenceJa: 全てが華と散った
findings.governingReading: all scattered like blossoms
findings.explanation: The English conveys destruction but removes the elegiac flower image governing the legend’s account of Camlann.

findings.highlight: The knights who sided with her died
findings.evidenceJa: 自分に付き従ってくれた騎士たちも散り
findings.governingReading: The knights who still followed her were scattered.
findings.explanation: The English asserts death where the source describes the remaining loyal force dispersing or falling away.

findings.highlight: her body was crippled
findings.evidenceJa: 自身の体も、傷ついて動かなかった
findings.governingReading: her own wounded body would no longer move
findings.explanation: Crippled converts an immediate battlefield condition into a categorical disability.

findings.highlight: She has no regrets. If there is one regret
findings.evidenceJa: 後悔などしていない。無念があるとしたら
findings.governingReading: She has no personal regret; if anything remains unfulfilled, it is the ruined country.
findings.explanation: The English uses regret for both terms and contradicts itself, erasing the distinction between remorse over her choice and grief at an unfinished duty.

findings.highlight: Strength escapes her shoulders.
findings.evidenceJa: 肩の力が抜ける
findings.governingReading: The tension leaves her shoulders.
findings.explanation: The literal calque obscures the first physical release that precedes Arturia voluntarily letting go of the sword.

findings.highlight: that is the end of her memories
findings.evidenceJa: 彼女の記憶には、この先などない
findings.governingReading: Her memories contain nothing beyond this point.
findings.explanation: The English can suggest a loss or termination of memory rather than the fact that her lived experience has not proceeded past the suspended instant.

findings.highlight: It’s not a shower or a drizzle, but just normal rain.
findings.evidenceJa: 小雨ではないが大降りではない、という、ありきたりの雨のようだ
findings.governingReading: The additional classification of the rain is commented out; the active page ends after noting that the rain is not very loud.
findings.explanation: mirror moon restores deleted weather narration and also muddles its contrast by making “shower” the opposite of drizzle.

findings.highlight: I rattle my teeth at the sudden headache.
findings.evidenceJa: 突然の頭痛に歯を鳴らした
findings.governingReading: The entire page describing a sudden brief headache and intrusive image is commented out.
findings.explanation: mirror moon restores a deleted page of bodily distress and changes the active awakening sequence.

findings.highlight: I grit my teeth loudly and suppress the urge to have a fit.
findings.evidenceJa: このまま歯が砕けても構わないっていうぐらい歯を鳴らして
findings.governingReading: The added teeth-shattering and violent-outburst description is commented out.
findings.explanation: mirror moon restores deleted escalation and renders 暴れ出す as the minimizing, juvenile “have a fit.”

findings.highlight: Just remembering it makes me mad.
findings.evidenceJa: 思い返すだけで気がヘンになる
findings.governingReading: Merely remembering it makes him feel as if he is losing his mind.
findings.explanation: Mad is read as angry, flattening destabilization into the anger already stated separately.

findings.highlight: nobody knew about it
findings.evidenceJa: 最後まで理解されなかった
findings.governingReading: She was not understood to the very end.
findings.explanation: The English changes Arturia’s defining lack of human understanding into simple failure to know about her efforts.

findings.highlight: Such easy words won’t fix anything.
findings.evidenceJa: そんな簡単な言葉で、埋められる物などない
findings.governingReading: No void like this can be filled with such easy words.
findings.explanation: Fix anything generalizes away the emotional deficit Shirou says praise cannot fill.

findings.highlight: her life must be repaid
findings.evidenceJa: その人生を清算させる
findings.governingReading: Her life must finally be settled so that she receives the happiness her struggle is owed.
findings.explanation: Life must be repaid is opaque English and risks making Arturia herself sound like a debt rather than the beneficiary of an overdue reckoning.

findings.highlight: I’ve been living trying to be a superhero
findings.evidenceJa: 正義の味方になると生きてきた
findings.governingReading: He has lived intending to become a hero of justice.
findings.explanation: mirror moon again replaces the work-defining justice ideal with the generic superhero category.

findings.highlight: realize my own distortions
findings.evidenceJa: 自らの歪さを思い知った
findings.governingReading: He is forced to recognize how warped he himself is.
findings.explanation: The plural abstraction weakens Shirou’s recognition of a single governing deformation in how he has lived.
